affected_system: rights-preserving compliance assistance, incentives, inspections, and enforcement
alternatives: compare eligible treated and credible untreated units for randomized or phased compliance assistance and incentive
estimate pre-specified overall and distributional effects of randomized or phased compliance assistance and incentive
pair randomized encouragement or threshold-based policy evaluation with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Eligibility, notice, awareness, capability, action, inspection, violation, sanction, and outcome remain distinct.
No behavioral score automatically triggers enforcement, benefit denial, or coercive action.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
baseline: retain pre-intervention conditions for randomized or phased compliance assistance and incentive.

constraints.description: The compliance, incentives, and behavioral policy evaluate must respect declared pre-specified assignment, comparison, outcome, spillover, and subgroup rules.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
decision_owner: regulatory operations director and behavioral insights lead
decision_question: Did randomized or phased assistance improve verified lawful completion without burden or coercion?

independence_key.binding_constraint: The compliance, incentives, and behavioral policy evaluate must respect declared pre-specified assignment, comparison, outcome, spillover, and subgroup rules.
independence_key.decision_object: randomized or phased compliance assistance and incentive
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for randomized or phased compliance assistance and incentive passes documented checks for dated assignment, comparison validity, pre-trends, outcome panels, attrition, spillovers, and falsification tests.
independence_key.intervention_mechanism: randomized encouragement or threshold-based policy evaluation
independence_key.primary_outcome: change in verified timely lawful completion and administrative burden

intended_claim: A versioned evaluate design for comparing declared alternatives affecting randomized or phased compliance assistance and incentive, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: change in verified timely lawful completion and administrative burden
distributional gap in change in verified timely lawful completion and administrative burden
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not infer intent, welfare, deterrence, or durable behavior from one administrative completion outcome.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for randomized or phased compliance assistance and incentive passes documented checks for dated assignment, comparison validity, pre-trends, outcome panels, attrition, spillovers, and falsification tests.

title: Evaluate compliance assistance and incentives
transportability_risks: Law, administrative burden, trust, incentives, capability, enforcement, and baseline behavior differ.
Observed compliance may reflect detection and documentation rather than underlying behavior.
